subtopics.title: ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026
subtopics.summary: The 10th edition of the biennial ICC Women's T20 tournament was held from 12 June to 5 July 2026, hosted by the England and Wales Cricket Board across 7 venues. The 12 teams played a round-robin group stage in 2 groups of 6, and the top 2 from each group reached the semi-finals. Australia beat England in the final at Lord's to win its record-extending 7th title.
facts: 10th edition of the biennial ICC Women's T20 International Cricket Tournament
Held 12 June to 5 July 2026; hosted by England and Wales Cricket Board across 7 venues
12 teams played in 2 groups of 6 in a round-robin format
Top 2 from each group advanced to the semi-finals
Final at Lord's Cricket Ground, London: Australia defeated England
Australia won its record-extending 7th title
Shree Charani (India): leading wicket-taker with 14 wickets
Charani set a national record for most wickets by an Indian in a single edition
Beth Mooney (Australia): Player of the Final and Player of the Tournament

subtopics.title: Sports and Youth Milestones
subtopics.summary: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced that Telangana will host the 8th Khelo India Youth Games in November 2026. Leander Paes was appointed Player Ambassador of the Asian Tennis Federation. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became India's youngest international cricket debutant at 15 years 99 days.
facts: Telangana to host the 8th Khelo India Youth Games, scheduled for November 2026 (announced by Mansukh Mandaviya's ministry)
7th Khelo India Youth Games were hosted by Bihar in 2025
Maharashtra was overall champion at the 7th KIYG, followed by Haryana and Rajasthan
Leander Paes appointed Player Ambassador of the Asian Tennis Federation to promote grassroots tennis
Paes is India's only tennis player to win an Olympic medal: Bronze in Men's Singles, 1996 Atlanta
Paes honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award (Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award)
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: India's youngest international cricket debutant at 15 years 99 days
Sooryavanshi made his senior T20I debut against England at Old Trafford, Manchester
Sooryavanshi broke Shafali Verma's record (15 years 239 days, against South Africa in 2019)

subtopics.title: Indian Monsoon
subtopics.summary: The monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds that brings major changes in rainfall, and India receives about 75 per cent of its annual rainfall during it. The southwest monsoon runs from June to September and has an Arabian Sea branch and a Bay of Bengal branch. Jet streams influence the monsoon's onset, strength and withdrawal.
facts: Monsoon: a seasonal reversal of winds bringing significant changes in rainfall; word from Arabic 'Mausim' (season)
India receives about 75% of its annual rainfall during the monsoon
Southwest Monsoon: June to September; Northeast Monsoon: October to December
Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats and causes heavy rainfall on the west coast
Bay of Bengal branch moves towards Northeast India and brings rainfall to the Ganga plains
In summer, land heats faster than water: low pressure over N. India, high pressure over the Indian Ocean
Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and force monsoon winds to shed moisture over India
Jet streams influence the onset, strength and withdrawal of the monsoon
El Nino (warming of Pacific Ocean waters) can weaken the Indian monsoon and reduce rainfall
Excess rainfall causes floods; weak monsoons lead to water shortages and droughts

subtopics.title: Paizhen Fault and the Medog Project
subtopics.summary: Chinese geologists raised safety concerns over the Medog (Yarlung Tsangpo) Hydropower Project because the active Paizhen Fault lies in the project's reservoir area. The fault is an active tectonic fault in the eastern Himalayan region of south-eastern Tibet and is part of a fault system created by the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates. The Yarlung Tsangpo changes its name as it flows from Tibet into India, becoming the Siang and then the Brahmaputra, and finally the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
facts: Chinese geologists raised safety concerns over the Medog (Yarlung Tsangpo) Hydropower Project
The concern is linked to the active Paizhen Fault in Tibet
Paizhen Fault: an active tectonic fault in the eastern Himalayan region of south-eastern Tibet
The fault passes through the reservoir area of the Medog project
It forms part of a fault system created by the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates
Yarlung Tsangpo originates in Tibet
Enters India through Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang River
Flows through Assam as the Brahmaputra
Enters Bangladesh as the Jamuna River

subtopics.title: Policy, Heritage and Observances
subtopics.summary: The Centre released a draft of CAFE-III norms that would tighten fuel-efficiency and CO2 emission standards for passenger vehicles from April 2027. Sushruta, the ancient Indian physician and surgeon, is known as the Father of Surgery, and his bronze statue was unveiled by Scotland's Royal College of Surgeons. July also carries several observances, including the International Day of Cooperatives and World Population Day.
facts: CAFE stands for Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency
CAFE norms were introduced by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency in 2017
Applies to petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG, hybrid and electric passenger vehicles weighing up to 3,500 kg
Draft CAFE-III norms propose stricter fuel-efficiency and CO2 standards for passenger vehicles from April 2027
Sushruta: Father of Surgery and Father of Plastic Surgery; disciple of Dhanvantari
Sushruta authored the Sushruta Samhita; it is part of Ayurveda's Great Trilogy with the Charaka Samhita and Astanga Hridaya
Sushruta's bronze statue was unveiled by Scotland's Royal College of Surgeons
International Day of Cooperatives: 1st Saturday of July; 2026 theme 'Cooperatives for a Peaceful World'
National Statistics Day: 29 June, honouring Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis; 2026 theme 'Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data'
World Population Day: 11 July; 2026 theme 'Realizing the Hopes and Aspirations of Young People - Today and for the Future'

quizzes.passage: The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 was one of the major events in the international cricket calendar, bringing national women's teams together in the Twenty20 format. The tournament was held over several weeks and was staged across a number of venues. Understanding how the event was structured helps explain how the final was reached. Two groups formed the opening phase. Each group contained the same number of teams, and every side played the other teams in its group in a round-robin format. The results of this phase determined which teams moved into the knockout rounds, where each match carried greater significance. The final was the last match of the competition. Individual players were also recognised with awards for their performances across the event. The tournament was organised by one national board, which worked with local venues to stage the matches. Several sides travelled to different grounds during the event, and supporters followed the progress of each team through the group stage and the knockout rounds. Players from many countries took part, giving the competition an international character. Results in the group phase were therefore central to the outcome of the event. Each stage of the event involved a defined set of fixtures.
